publication_rule: Only values tied to a named primary official source and an explicit reference period are promoted to the dashboard. Unverified or methodologically incompatible values remain withheld.

JOR.headline: What do we know now, and what exactly does each Jordanian statistic measure?
JOR.dek: Jordan is the first complete country room. It combines current official indicators with a source map, measurement notes, a preservation ledger and two Lab findings built from public Jordanian evidence.

indicators.definition: All-items consumer price index, annual percentage change; current 2018=100 series.

indicators.label: CPI monthly change
indicators.definition: Month-on-month change in headline CPI.

indicators.label: Unemployment
indicators.definition: Dashboard promotion withheld until the current total-population release is archived with its denominator and release date.

indicators.label: Labour-force participation
indicators.definition: Participation is reported relative to the population aged 15+; current value not promoted without a preserved source release.

indicators.label: Real GDP growth
indicators.definition: Current value withheld pending a directly archived official national-accounts release.

indicators.label: Policy rate
indicators.definition: Current policy-rate value is not promoted until the underlying CBJ decision notice is preserved.

sources.release: General government finance / debt / budget reporting

measurement_notes.question: Annual inflation rose after monthly price pressure had started cooling. Contradiction?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Year-on-year CPI compares each month with the same month a year earlier, while month-on-month CPI compares adjacent months. The windows can move differently because of base effects and the full prior-year path.

measurement_notes.question: Is CPI a direct cost-of-living index?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Jordan's statistical methodology describes CPI as a measure of price change. It should not be silently re-labelled as a household-specific cost-of-living measure.

measurement_notes.question: Which Jordanian unemployment rate are you quoting?
measurement_notes.answer: The official labour system distinguishes Jordanians and non-Jordanians, and current outputs can report a total-population measure. A headline number is incomplete without the population perimeter, age framework and denominator.

measurement_notes.question: Can a 2026 CPI release be compared with any older Jordan series without checking metadata?
measurement_notes.answer: Not automatically. The current published CPI series uses 2018=100. Base-period and basket changes must be recorded before joining historical files.

measurement_notes.question: What did users actually know at the time?
measurement_notes.answer: A current historical table can differ from what was available on the original release date. The ledger therefore preserves release date, reference period and original-source pointer separately.

findings.title: The annual inflation rate was still rising after monthly price pressure had begun easing.
findings.body: Jordan's headline CPI rose from 1.06% y/y in January to 2.83% in May 2026, even though month-on-month price growth had already varied substantially across the period. By June, the annual rate eased slightly to 2.79% and the monthly rate to 0.14%.
findings.why: The finding is about measurement windows, not a causal claim. Annual and monthly inflation answer different questions.

findings.title: Which Jordanian unemployment rate are you quoting?
findings.body: Jordanian labour-market outputs distinguish population perimeters including Jordanians and non-Jordanians. A single unemployment figure can therefore conceal a denominator and population-scope choice that matters for comparison.
findings.why: This is a Same Label, Different Statistic problem: the label 'unemployment' is not enough metadata.

EGY.headline: Which Egyptian inflation rate?
EGY.dek: Egypt's room starts with the perimeter problem: urban headline CPI, national CPI concepts and CBE core inflation are different statistical objects. The page keeps those objects separate and preserves the chain from CAPMAS production to CBE policy use.

indicators.label: Core inflation
indicators.definition: CBE-calculated core measure. Value withheld until the current release is preserved alongside the methodology note.

indicators.label: Unemployment
indicators.definition: Labour-force survey measure for the Egyptian civilian labour force inside Egypt; current value not promoted without archived release metadata.

indicators.label: Labour-force participation
indicators.definition: Participation measure tied to CAPMAS labour-force survey population and age framework.

indicators.label: Real GDP growth

measurement_notes.question: Urban headline, national headline or core inflation?
measurement_notes.answer: They are not interchangeable. CAPMAS produces CPI releases across geographic concepts; the CBE's policy target is tied to urban headline inflation, while the CBE calculates core inflation separately.

measurement_notes.question: What does the headline urban rate leave out?
measurement_notes.answer: The label itself identifies a geographic perimeter. A national welfare claim cannot be inferred from an urban headline rate without checking the underlying coverage.

measurement_notes.question: Why can year-on-year inflation accelerate when current monthly price pressure is modest?
measurement_notes.answer: Because the annual rate depends on the comparison month a year earlier. The room treats base effects as an explicit measurement object rather than a narrative afterthought.

measurement_notes.question: Did rebasing change the historical series?
measurement_notes.answer: The current CPI series uses FY2018/19 as base year with weights from the FY2017/18 household survey. Historical joins across prior bases require a vintage and methodology map.

measurement_notes.question: Where does a media inflation number actually come from?
measurement_notes.answer: The source tree is CAPMAS statistical production → CBE headline/core policy presentation → downstream IMF, World Bank and media reuse. The room preserves that hierarchy.

ledger.revised: No revision observed in source consulted

findings.title: The phrase “Egyptian inflation” hides a geographic choice.
findings.body: Egypt's policy-facing headline measure is urban headline inflation. A national CPI concept and a CBE core measure answer different questions and should not be merged into one generic inflation series.
findings.why: The statistical perimeter is part of the number. Geography belongs in the citation, not only in the methodology appendix.

findings.title: Headline and core inflation are separate analytical objects.
findings.body: CAPMAS produces the headline CPI input while the Central Bank of Egypt calculates core inflation separately. Divergence between the two can be informative, but only after their construction and exclusions are kept explicit.
findings.why: A policy narrative that silently switches between headline and core inflation can manufacture a trend that is not present in either series alone.

SAU.headline: Did the economy change, or did the measurement system change?
SAU.dek: Saudi Arabia's room foregrounds documented methodology breaks: the Labour Force Survey redesign from Q1 2025, census-based population-series transitions and a CPI system with updated classifications and chain-linked weights.

indicators.label: Headline CPI
indicators.definition: Current all-items CPI, 2023=100; value withheld until a directly preserved monthly release is attached.

indicators.label: Unemployment
indicators.definition: Labour-market rate subject to the Q1 2025 survey redesign and population-series documentation.

indicators.label: Labour-force participation
indicators.definition: Participation rate; comparison across the Q1 2025 methodology break requires explicit treatment.

indicators.label: Real GDP growth
indicators.definition: Official national-accounts growth; current value withheld pending frozen release.

indicators.label: Policy rate
indicators.definition: SAMA policy rates; current value withheld until decision notice is archived.

indicators.label: FX regime
indicators.definition: Longstanding riyal-US dollar peg reference; transaction quotes can vary around the official parity.

indicators.label: CPI index base
indicators.definition: Current CPI presentation with updated consumption classification and chain-linked weight methodology.

indicators.label: Labour-method break
indicators.definition: New questionnaire detail and employment-status standard changes begin in Q1 2025 documentation.

sources.release: Labour Market Statistics / Labour Force Survey
Policy rates, exchange rates, monetary statistics

measurement_notes.question: Did unemployment change, or did measurement change?
measurement_notes.answer: The Labour Force Survey was redesigned from Q1 2025. A break analysis must separate genuine labour-market movement from questionnaire and classification changes.

measurement_notes.question: Are all historical Saudi labour observations on the same population frame?
measurement_notes.answer: No. GASTAT documentation identifies different census-based population series across historical periods, including 1992, 2004, 2010 and 2022 census bases.

measurement_notes.question: Is the current CPI basket fixed forever?
measurement_notes.answer: No. The current CPI methodology uses annually updated chain-linked weights and presents the index as 2023=100 under updated consumption classifications.

measurement_notes.question: Saudi or non-Saudi labour indicator?
measurement_notes.answer: Nationality is a first-order perimeter choice in Saudi labour statistics. Nationality-specific and total indicators should not be collapsed into a single trend.

measurement_notes.question: Survey employment or administrative employment?
measurement_notes.answer: Survey-based labour status and administrative employment records measure different constructs. Differences between them are an evidence object, not automatically an error.

findings.title: A labour-market break starts in Q1 2025.
findings.body: GASTAT documents a Labour Force Survey redesign beginning in Q1 2025, including questionnaire changes and updates connected to international employment-status standards. Pre/post comparisons therefore require a methodology flag.
findings.why: A clean-looking unemployment time series can be analytically dirty if the measurement system changes underneath it.

findings.title: Saudi inflation weights are designed to move.
findings.body: The current CPI methodology uses chain-linked, annually updated weights with a 2023=100 presentation and updated consumption classifications. The basket is not a timeless fixed object.
findings.why: Long-horizon inflation comparison needs methodology/version metadata, not only index values.

MAR.dek: Morocco is the Lab's first bilingual-provenance room. HCP's new 2026 employment survey introduces explicit conceptual and design changes, so the page preserves French source terminology and flags non-comparability with the older ENE series.

measurement_notes.question: Can Q1 2026 unemployment be pasted onto the old ENE series?
measurement_notes.answer: No. HCP explicitly states that the new strict-unemployment concept under EMO2026 is not directly comparable with the previous ENE unemployment series.

measurement_notes.question: Unemployment versus underemployment?
measurement_notes.answer: They capture different labour-market conditions. Underemployment should remain a separate indicator rather than being folded into unemployment.

measurement_notes.question: Urban and rural labour markets: one Morocco rate?
measurement_notes.answer: National aggregates can hide large geographic structure. The room preserves urban/rural dimensions when source tables support them.

measurement_notes.question: Who counts as economically active?
measurement_notes.answer: Participation and unemployment depend on the activity-status framework. The 2026 survey redesign makes those definitions part of the time-series metadata.

measurement_notes.question: Why preserve French terminology?
measurement_notes.answer: Translation can silently erase distinctions in official concepts. The room stores French original labels and adds English explanatory metadata instead of replacing the source language.

findings.title: Morocco's Q1 2026 unemployment rate belongs to a new measurement regime.
findings.body: HCP's EMO2026 introduces a new employment survey framework and explicitly warns that strict unemployment under the new system is not directly comparable with the older ENE unemployment series.
findings.why: A graph can show a false jump or improvement if a methodology break is treated as an economic event.

findings.title: Bilingual provenance is part of statistical accuracy.
findings.body: Morocco's official evidence base is rich in French-language source material. The Lab preserves original terminology while adding English metadata, allowing users to inspect the source concept rather than relying on a flattened translation.
findings.why: Some comparability errors begin in translation before they reach the spreadsheet.

measurement_notes.question: Federal UAE CPI or Dubai CPI?
measurement_notes.answer: They answer different geographic questions. Dubai's CPI metadata defines the reference area as the Emirate of Dubai; it cannot be substituted for federal UAE inflation.

measurement_notes.question: Where does Abu Dhabi fit?
measurement_notes.answer: SCAD publishes Abu Dhabi-specific CPI, labour, trade and other statistics. Those are emirate-level evidence, not duplicate federal releases.

measurement_notes.question: Which rate is “right”?
measurement_notes.answer: The useful question is which perimeter matches the research question. A Dubai household-cost question and a federal macro question require different statistical objects.

measurement_notes.question: Can publication lags differ across the three systems?
measurement_notes.answer: Yes. Federal and emirate agencies have different release calendars. The planned lag audit records reference period and publication date for each perimeter.

measurement_notes.question: Can historical coverage be joined automatically?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Federal, Dubai and Abu Dhabi series can have different base years, start dates and metadata. The coverage matrix will record those boundaries before any merge.

ledger.first: FCSC + Dubai + Abu Dhabi mapped separately

findings.title: “UAE inflation” can refer to different geographic statistical objects.
findings.body: The federal statistical system, Dubai's statistical authority and Abu Dhabi's SCAD all publish economic statistics. A number quoted without its geographic perimeter can answer a different question from the one the reader thinks is being answered.
findings.why: The geography belongs in the variable name. 'CPI' alone is insufficient metadata in a federal statistical system with major emirate-level producers.

findings.title: The UAE's statistical architecture is itself evidence infrastructure.
findings.body: FCSC provides federal statistics while Dubai and Abu Dhabi maintain deep emirate-level systems. The Lab maps the institutional source tree first, then compares values only where definitions and geography genuinely align.
findings.why: Source architecture prevents false comparisons before they enter a model, memo or chart.
